schema_version: v0 — migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
owner: akiendelllinux_cc_0 (CC) gates writes to the code and proofs. Akien owns the design — the anatomy, 'the questions are the sieve', proximity-not-cost as the coarseness axis, and bands-over-strict-numbering are his, ruled in conversation 2026-08-06 and routed here by him ('i believe it's /sorted ruled and otherwise approved').
intention: build_inspector stops being a hand-rolled gate beside a bolted-on nexus and becomes what it already is by anatomy: a learning block whose CONSTRAINING QUESTIONS ARE ITS SIEVES. Two moves. (1) A sieve's MESH is DERIVED from its own reach — computed from what it imports and opens through import_sieve's graph, never authored — and the nest orders itself by those bands. A FINDING CARRIES A DATUM AND A SCORE — the datum is what was looked at, the score is a float that means nothing alone and everything against the sieve's own mesh, which is the requirement it is relative to. Binary today: every score is 1.0 or 0.0 and every mesh is `>= 1`, so a nest of five reads [1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0] = 0.0. NO THIRD VALUE ANYWHERE — a sieve that never ran because a coarser band caught is ABSENT from the report, with the stopping band named once, because 0.0 would assert 'did not catch', a claim it is not entitled to make. (2) The inspector's checks become a declared data-only block spec and run on the learning_block engine, candidates loop degenerate at one candidate (the component under inspection), the engine untouched and branchless.
why: Akien opened it as a contradiction, in his words: 'Inspector is supposed to be a learning block, which would imply it's questions need to be in a tree and not in filters/seives... unless the seives and nest were implemented in the trees?' The contradiction dissolves, and what it exposes underneath is the real defect. The anatomy (decisions/2026-08-05-a-learning-block-is-a-question-nexus-rebased) names a domain KB and constraining questions and DOES NOT SAY WHERE THEY LIVE — his words today: 'that definition does not say where they are... the questions are the rigid part, they can be in a dict... that's just part of the kb that isn't in a tree.' So a rigid dict was never disqualifying. What disqualifies build_inspector is that it does not run on the engine at all: it carries its own inspect() over a flat FILTERS dict, with nexus.py alongside as a separate growth path, so the block learns right up to the moment a check is installed and then stops. Nothing can say 'this sieve has caught nothing in forty builds.' THE LIVED SYMPTOM IS AKIEN'S, and it is the one he has now named twice: he reads the system's own gate and finds it is not built the way the system says gates are built — a check whose strictness lives in a human's head, in an assembly whose order lives in a hand-written list, inside a device that claims to be a learning block. The second symptom is quieter and worse: a hand-labeled nest goes stale silently. Edit a sieve so it reaches the network and it keeps running near the top forever, because the label still reads what it read the day it was written.

falsifier: FALSIFIER, RED by physics on any of: (1) a mesh band is AUTHORED anywhere — a field, a constant, a docstring line — rather than derived from the sieve's own code; (2) editing a sieve so it reaches further does not move its band at the next derivation; (3) a sieve in a finer band emits a score for an input a coarser band already caught — it must be ABSENT from the report, never 0.0, because 0.0 is a claim it cannot make (Law 7: a record of truth does not collapse an unanswerable question into an answer); (3b) a score appears without the mesh it is relative to, which turns a verdict back into an uninterpretable reading; (4) the nest fires one sieve, reads it, and re-fires, rather than shaking once; (5) the engine grows a build_inspector-specific branch. WRONG-INTENT TELL: if deriving reach needs per-sieve exceptions, 'reach is derivable' is falsified — stop and reconcile, do not accrete cases.
horizon: Re-read at the first sieve whose reach the derivation cannot compute, and at child (a)'s opening band-sorting pass. If the existing checks do not separate into bands, the domain is flatter than the metaphor and this node re-enters design rather than taking a patch.
distinctions_recorded: PROXIMITY, NOT COMPUTATION TIME, is the coarseness axis — Akien's correction, verbatim: 'not computation time as in your example. it'd be more like how deep we have to look. is it a file lookup? is it a value in a file? is it a value i have to compute from multiple local sources? do i need the web? --- more related to proximity?' CC had proposed cost, which comes apart from coarseness in software: a coarse check can walk the whole repo and a fine one can be a regex on a line. Proximity is a property of the sieve; cost is a property of the run.

MESH-AS-PHRASING vs MESH-AS-BAND are two things wearing one word, and Akien drew the line the same day. 'Ask the finest requirement possible' — his example: ask whether a keyword is available, not what Python version is running — is about how a sieve is PHRASED. The band is about how far it must REACH. Merging them is the failure this distinction is filed against.

FOUR BANDS, BOUNDARIES WHERE THE FAILURE MODE CHANGES, not where the milliseconds change: input-in-hand (cannot fail environmentally) / local disk (fails on absence) / correlated local work — several files, git plumbing, an AST walk — (fails on inconsistency) / off-box — db, inference host, network — (fails on UNAVAILABILITY, which nothing above it can do). That last boundary earns its keep: an unreachable host must never be able to mask a local finding. THE COUNT IS A FIRST CUT given at Akien's explicit request for CC's experience, and it is a hypothesis (Law 3) until the sorting pass runs.

BANDS, NOT STRICT NUMBERING — rejected on ownership, not taste: inserting a sieve between 2 and 3 forces fractional numbers or renumbering, and renumbering is a WRITE TO OTHER SIEVES (Law 6). With bands a new sieve declares its own and the nest reassembles; nothing existing is touched. Within a band, order genuinely does not matter, which is what lets a band be shaken at once.

THE SIEVE KNOWS NOTHING ABOUT THE NEST and the nest reads nothing but the sieve's own code — Akien named the payoff: 'it's a charactaristic of the kind of thing it's doing rather than where it's doing it. greater reusability.' There is no configuration surface between sieve and assembly at all, so the same sieve dropped into another nest self-places.

CC REIFIED AN EXAMPLE, caught by Akien at n=1 in the same conversation: his mesh illustration (exists -> non-empty -> valid JSON -> field present -> in range) was shipped by CC as a five-tier taxonomy and a definition of coarseness. 'that was an example, not a definition of truth.' Same tell as the trigger-kinds enum and the rack — a list of instances turned into a closed set.

A BAND SEQUENCES, IT NEVER FORBIDS — Akien's correction 2026-08-06, and it is the second time in one day CC wrote a current state as a law. The band exists so that a distant sieve runs LAST and an unreachable host cannot mask a local finding; it does not exist to red a sieve for reaching. An EMPTY band is empty, not closed. The distinguisher, from the same day's self-inspection ruling: does this describe how the world must be, or what we have not built yet?

A FINDING CARRIES A DATUM AND A SCORE — Akien, 2026-08-06, closing the shape: 'each finding can have a datum AND a score. because the score is relative to the requirement.' That sentence is why the float is worth having and why it is not ambiguous: a bare number would be a reading, not a verdict, and the mesh is what makes it a verdict. It also places the learnable value exactly where the design already wanted it — the mesh is the number a block can move on feedback (learns-its-gates), and the score is the measurement it moves against. BINARY TODAY BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY LAW: every check build_inspector runs is binary as of now, so every score is 1.0 or 0.0 and every mesh is `>= 1`. His stated expiry — 'this may change later based on things like elapsed time or performacne values' — so the float is forward-shape for a named future, not speculative generality. Recorded this way deliberately: a CURRENT LIMITATION written as a limitation, never as a rule, which is the correction he made on this same day about self-inspection.

THE TWO KINDS OF STACK ARE THE EVALUATION LOOP AND THE DECIDE STEP, and both are already built. Akien recalled that the filter era had two kinds of stack — 'one that would let one answer thru and one that would let a set of answers thru.' They are not two nest types: a nest shakes a SET of candidates through an ORDERED set of sieves, so 'a set through' is the survivors of the evaluation loop, and 'one through' is cairn/learning_block/engine.py:175's DECIDE OR ESCALATE, which ranks survivors by the spec's order and picks one. THE VECTOR AND THE FILE-LIST ARE TWO MARGINALS OF ONE TABLE: roll up along the candidate axis and you get his [1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0] = 0.0; roll up along the sieve axis and you get what each mesh caught, which is the 'list a file for each finding' shape. build_inspector is already the many-candidates case — components are the candidates, checks are the sieves — and the single-component vector is one slice of it. CC's read, not Akien's ruling, but it describes code that exists rather than proposing a mechanism.

THE ROLL-UP RULE IS THE FRAGILE PART, not the vector. Rolling a candidate's scores up with AND treats every sieve as must-pass, which is correct for a checklist gate and is what build_inspector is. The first ADVISORY sieve — one whose failure should inform without condemning — breaks the roll-up rule and nothing else. Named here so that when it arrives it is recognised as a rule change rather than patched as a special case.

THE RENAME IS OUT OF BOUNDS. decisions/2026-08-06-a-stack-of-sieves-is-a-nest also renames filter->sieve corpus-wide and carries its own sequencing clause — before or after nothing-rides-loose, never during. This node uses the vocabulary and performs no rename; a child that quietly does so is out of bounds.

measured_at_cast: cairn/learning_block/engine.py:169 — `killed_by = [con['name'] for con in spec['constraints'] if ...]`. The evaluation loop already runs EVERY constraint against each candidate in one pass and records EVERY one that killed it. So ONE SHAKE and THE GRADATION are already built and block-general; the nest's only missing pieces are the BANDING and the not-applicable value. This is why child (a) is a small change in learning_block rather than a new mechanism in build_inspector, and it is the first evidence for the reading — CC's, not Akien's — that the nest IS the learning block's evaluation loop rather than an inspector-local device.

sorting_pass_2026_08_06.what_ran: Child (a)'s opening move, the pass the cast said was allowed to come back flat: derive every FILTERS entry's reach from its own code and see whether the checks separate into bands. Function-level AST over cairn/build_inspector/inspector.py, transitive through in-module helpers.
sorting_pass_2026_08_06.result: 18 checks. THREE bands populated, not four: in-hand 3 (charter_on_disk, proofs_exist, silent_device), local-disk 2 (state_is_projection, forwarding_order_resolves), correlated-local 13 (every chart-packet judge), off-box 0.
sorting_pass_2026_08_06.the_domain_is_flatter_than_the_metaphor: 13 of 18 in one band, so FINE-GRAINED ORDERING BUYS ALMOST NOTHING and the four-band first cut was one band too many for what exists. The node is not falsified — it is right-sized. What survives is smaller and better: the coarse band is a PRECONDITION GATE, and that is the payoff. Today a component with no charter still generates thirteen findings about its chart packets; banded, those thirteen go ABSENT rather than noisy, which is the whole not-applicable rule doing real work on real output.
sorting_pass_2026_08_06.the_off_box_band_is_empty_and_that_is_no: CC first proposed a tooth that would RED an off-box sieve in the build gate, and Akien refused it as a current state written as a law — the same correction he made that morning about self-inspection, repeated by CC in the same session. THERE ARE ALREADY TWO HOSTS (this box and Hex), and in TheIgors era FOUR laptops, each with a copy of the database (this box master, the rest failover), each running one Igor instance with four centers of awareness against local 3b/7b Ollama on ten-minute timeouts, overnight. His words: 'will we do that? I don't know. but we CAN.' So the off-box band's job is SEQUENCING, NOT PROHIBITION: when an off-box sieve arrives it runs last, and an unreachable host cannot mask a local finding. The emptiness is a fact about today's corpus, never a rule about the world. NOTE THE FIT: the learning-block anatomy already reserves the slot — candidate questions come from feedback and LLM processing 'probably in the evenings' — and a slow local host on a ten-minute budget is exactly what an evening pass is for. The expensive sieves run off-box overnight, the cheap ones at every crossing, and the band is what keeps the two from being confused.
sorting_pass_2026_08_06.how_the_derivation_must_work_measured_th: V1 WAS A COIN-TOSS RED and is kept because it is evidence. Matching on call-name tails put 15 of 18 off-box: Path.resolve() and inference_domain.resolve() share a tail, dict.get() looks like an HTTP get. Reach must be anchored on what each alias actually IMPORTS, resolved from the module's own import statements. THIS IS ALSO WHY import_sieve CANNOT BE REUSED AS-IS: its graph is module-granular and a sieve is a FUNCTION, so the function-level walk is new work that sits on top of the existing graph rather than beside it.

[CORPUS] IS THE NEST BLOCK-GENERAL OR INSPECTOR-LOCAL? CC's read is that a nest IS the learning block's evaluation loop — coarse-first, one shake, survivors plus what killed each — and that the inspector is only the subclass where the survivors get named a finding. If block-general, sieve/mesh/nest is vocabulary for every block's second loop and child (a) belongs in learning_block; if inspector-local, it belongs in build_inspector and child (a) is smaller. Akien has not ruled it.

[CORPUS] IS BUILD_INSPECTOR'S CANDIDATES LOOP REALLY DEGENERATE? CC's read: one candidate, the component under inspection, so only the evaluation loop does work — which is why an inspector looks like a flat stack of checks. If false, child (b) is a larger migration than it is described as.
